**2. Water Conservation Proposal – Submitted by Mr. Arjun Deshpande (Agenda Item 4)**

Mr. Arjun Deshpande, a resident of Wing A, had submitted a detailed proposal titled "Water Conservation and Rainwater Harvesting Initiative" on 2 December 2023. The proposal was circulated to all committee members on 5 December 2023 for review prior to this meeting.

Mr. Deshpande presented the key points of his proposal to the committee:

- The society currently draws an average of 4.2 lakh litres of water per month from the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) supply, supplemented by two borewells.
- His proposal includes the installation of a rainwater harvesting system across the three residential towers (Wings A, B, and C) and the clubhouse terrace, with an estimated catchment area of approximately 1,850 square metres.
- The system would include underground storage tanks (two tanks of 20,000 litres each), filtration units, and piping to direct harvested water to the garden irrigation line and the cooling tower of the central air-conditioning system in the clubhouse.
- The estimated capital cost is ₹ 8,75,000, with an additional annual maintenance cost of approximately ₹ 45,000.
- He estimated that the system could capture and reuse around 2.6 lakh litres of water annually, reducing dependence on PMC supply by approximately 5–7% and lowering the society's monthly water bill by ₹ 6,000–₹ 8,000.

Mr. Suresh Kumar from the Maintenance Office noted that he had verified the roof drainage points and confirmed that the terrace drain outlets in all three wings are in working condition. He also mentioned that the clubhouse terrace has two additional drain points that could be connected to the proposed system, though one of these is partially blocked and would require clearing before installation.

The Treasurer, Mrs. Farah Khan, raised a concern about the availability of funds. She noted that the society's capital reserve fund currently stands at ₹ 42 lakhs, but a portion of this is earmarked for the scheduled lift modernisation project in Wing B and the boundary wall repair work. She suggested that the committee consider whether the water conservation project should be funded from the capital reserve or through a special levy on all members.

Mr. Nitin Joshi proposed that the committee form a small sub-committee to study the technical feasibility and cost details further, and to obtain at least two quotations from vendors specialising in rainwater harvesting systems. He suggested that Mr. Deshpande be invited to be part of this sub-committee, given his initiative.

**Discussion:** Mr. Vikram Patil supported the proposal in principle but noted that the society had faced a similar proposal in 2019 which had not been implemented due to concerns about the quality of harvested water during the monsoon. Mr. Deshpande responded that his proposal includes a three-stage filtration system and periodic water quality testing, which would address those earlier concerns.

**2. Water Conservation Proposal – Submitted by Mr. Arjun Deshpande (Agenda Item 4)**

Mr. Arjun Deshpande, a resident of Wing A, had submitted a detailed proposal titled "Water Conservation and Rainwater Harvesting Initiative" on 2 December 2023. The proposal was circulated to all committee members on 5 December 2023 for review prior to this meeting.

Mr. Deshpande presented the key points of his proposal to the committee:

- The society currently draws an average of 4.2 lakh litres of water per month from the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) supply, supplemented by two borewells.
- His proposal includes the installation of a rainwater harvesting system across the three residential towers (Wings A, B, and C) and the clubhouse terrace, with an estimated catchment area of approximately 1,850 square metres.
- The system would include underground storage tanks (two tanks of 20,000 litres each), filtration units, and piping to direct harvested water to the garden irrigation line and the cooling tower of the central air-conditioning system in the clubhouse.
- The estimated capital cost is ₹ 8,75,000, with an additional annual maintenance cost of approximately ₹ 45,000.
- He estimated that the system could capture and reuse around 2.6 lakh litres of water annually, reducing dependence on PMC supply by approximately 5–7% and lowering the society's monthly water bill by ₹ 6,000–₹ 8,000.

Mr. Suresh Kumar from the Maintenance Office noted that he had verified the roof drainage points and confirmed that the terrace drain outlets in all three wings are in working condition. He also mentioned that the clubhouse terrace has two additional drain points that could be connected to the proposed system, though one of these is partially blocked and would require clearing before installation.

The Treasurer, Mrs. Farah Khan, raised a concern about the availability of funds. She noted that the society's capital reserve fund currently stands at ₹ 42 lakhs, but a portion of this is earmarked for the scheduled lift modernisation project in Wing B and the boundary wall repair work. She suggested that the committee consider whether the water conservation project should be funded from the capital reserve or through a special levy on all members.

Mr. Nitin Joshi proposed that the committee form a small sub-committee to study the technical feasibility and cost details further, and to obtain at least two quotations from vendors specialising in rainwater harvesting systems. He suggested that Mr. Deshpande be invited to be part of this sub-committee, given his initiative.

**Discussion:** Mr. Vikram Patil supported the proposal in principle but noted that the society had faced a similar proposal in 2019 which had not been implemented due to concerns about the quality of harvested water during the monsoon. Mr. Deshpande responded that his proposal includes a three-stage filtration system and periodic water quality testing, which would address those earlier concerns.

TICKET ID: MNT-2024-0039
DATE & TIME: 05-Jan-2024, 11:30 IST
RESIDENT: Mr. Rajesh Iyer (A-1101)
DESCRIPTION: Lift No. 2 is making a grinding noise when it passes the 8th floor. Also, the door on the ground floor is closing too fast.
STATUS: Resolved
REMARKS: Vendor (Otis Service) attended on 06-Jan-2024. Found a worn-out guide roller and adjusted the door tension. Noise gone. Door closing speed reset to standard. Closed on 07-Jan-2024.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
TICKET ID: MNT-2024-0045
DATE & TIME: 11-Jan-2024, 16:45 IST
RESIDENT: Mr. Arjun Deshpande (C-304)
DESCRIPTION: Water pressure is very low in the entire flat, especially in the kitchen tap. The problem started after the morning supply. No leakage visible in my flat.
STATUS: In Progress
REMARKS: Checked the water meter and the inlet valve on the terrace. Found partial blockage in the strainer of the main inlet pipe for the C wing. Cleaning scheduled for 12-Jan-2024. Resident informed that pressure will be restored by evening.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
TICKET ID: MNT-2024-0048
DATE & TIME: 13-Jan-2024, 10:00 IST
RESIDENT: Mrs. Meera Nair (B-502)
DESCRIPTION: The exhaust fan in the common toilet on the 5th floor is not working. The switch is on but the fan is silent.
STATUS: Resolved

STATUS: Resolved

TICKET ID: MNT-2024-0061

RESIDENT: Mr. Rajesh Iyer (B-502)
DESCRIPTION: The geyser in the guest bathroom is not heating water. The indicator light comes on but the water stays cold.

DATE & TIME: 12-Feb-2024, 09:15 IST
RESIDENT: Mrs. Sunita Rao (A-1103)
DESCRIPTION: The main door lock of the flat is jammed. Key goes in but does not turn. Resident is locked out and waiting in the corridor.
STATUS: Resolved

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
TICKET ID: MNT-2024-0079
DATE & TIME: 18-Feb-2024, 14:30 IST
RESIDENT: Mr. Amit Shah (C-1204)
DESCRIPTION: The drainage pipe from the kitchen sink is leaking. Water is collecting in the cabinet below and there is a bad smell.
STATUS: Resolved
REMARKS: Found a crack in the PVC pipe near the joint. Replaced the pipe section and sealed all joints. No leakage after testing with water. Closed on 19-Feb-2024.

RESIDENT: Mrs. Kavita Joshi (B-704)

STATUS: Resolved

RESIDENT: Mrs. Meera Nair (C-1502)

STATUS: Resolved
